state.domain: An access campaign reviews one item per expected account-entitlement pair. Items independently own decisions. Existing policy requires an authoritative campaign completed fact only when all required items have closed. The architectural constraint prohibits a write decision that must collect or decide over every child, including a distributed chain or ledger. Projection reports may lag. Delegates and authorization remain separate owners.

per_item_report.instructions: If each access-review item independently records its final decision and a projection displays pending and decided items, does this alone prove an authoritative campaign-wide assertion that every required item has been decided?

all_child_gate.instructions: If a campaign completion write is permitted only after a process checks every required item outcome, does that write still depend on all children even if outcomes are stored on the items and streamed in pages?

distributed_ledger.instructions: If each selected item is tracked in a separate admission record and a process must traverse all of those records before sealing, is that still a distributed per-item ledger used to decide the parent write?

batch_reporting.instructions: Can individual privileged-safe access decisions be recorded independently while a non-authoritative report groups them by a shared user action identifier?

business_tradeoff.instructions: Does replacing an authoritative completed campaign with a projection of item statuses weaken the original guarantee that a durable campaign completion means all required items were closed?

cycle_edge.instructions: If a new graph edge is accepted only after checking whether an arbitrary path already connects its endpoints, can validation require examining an unbounded number of existing edges?
